_comment: Short 9 in docs/CONTENT.md: same day, same code is not a duplicate; same PERSON, same day, same code is. The Short that teaches when not to dispute.
_why_now: Made out of plan order. Of 68 audits in Firestore, duplicate_charge was the second most common finding (16 audits) after billed_vs_allowed_mismatch (53), while deductible_misapplied — Short 7's subject — never fired once.
_injury: Flu shots: two people, two sore arms. The only Short where nobody is hurt, which is why it can be the one that says 'this bill is fine'.
_numbers: One: a $40 flu shot, the same figure on both lines.
_trust: It teaches when NOT to dispute. A tool that only ever finds problems is a tool nobody believes; saying 'this one is fine' is what makes the other six worth listening to.

variants.shots: You and your daughter got flu shots on the same afternoon. The bill has two identical lines.

body.text: That is not a duplicate. Two people, two shots, two charges.
A duplicate is the same person, the same day, the same code, billed twice.
And two identical lines often have a reason. Two X-rays. One knee each side. A second dose.
So check the name on the line, check the date, and look for a reason there would be two.
If there is no reason, that is the line to ask about.
Your insurance letter is the tiebreaker. If it lists the charge once, the letter already agrees with you.
Check yours before you dispute. Or upload them free at UseClaimRight.com.
